_why: Everything a person keeps lives in their account (Hidde, 2026-09-02: 'alles wat wordt opgeslagen, moet op je account zijn'; again 2026-09-18: 'stop saving stuff locally anywhere ... always account related'). This file is the whole list of what either surface is still allowed to write to the device, one line of reason each. scripts/qa.py checks the website against it and scripts/localcheck.py checks the app. Adding a key here is a decision somebody has to write down; a key that is not here fails the push. A key built from a variable is refused outright on both surfaces, because a list can only read literals and a per-tree key cannot be enumerated to clear it.

web.ancienttrees_session: The account token. Not a saved thing: it is the thing that says whose account this is.
web.at_notrack: The analytics opt-out. Storing it in an account would mean needing an account to refuse being counted.
web.at_contribute_draft: Text somebody typed and has not sent. An unfinished sentence is not something they saved, and the magic-link round trip reloads the page under them.

app.measure.install.v1: The anonymous analytics id. It must NOT be the account: tying it to one would turn cookieless counting into tracking a person.
app.measure.queue.v1: Analytics events with nowhere to go yet. Unsent, like the web's draft, and dropped once they land.
app.reviewPrompt.fired.v2: Whether THIS install has asked for an App Store review. Apple's own limit is per install, so an account cannot answer it.
app.reviewPrompt.last.v2: When this install last asked, same reason.
app.reviewPrompt.seen.v1: Which payoff moments this install has already used, same reason.
app.nudge.fired.v1: Which nudges this phone has shown. Screen bookkeeping, not something a person keeps.
app.nudge.last.v1: When this phone last nudged, same reason.
app.directions.app: Which maps app to open. A fact about what is installed on THIS phone, not about the person.
app.hero.index.v1: Which of three bundled header pictures was shown last, so the next launch shows another.
app.ancienttrees.last_fix: The last GPS fix, so a cold launch can draw a map before Core Location answers. Never sent anywhere.
app.distanceUnit: An echo of profiles.units. The account is the truth: the launch task pulls it and every change pushes it back.
app.blocked-accounts: An echo of the blocks table. The server is the truth; the local copy makes a block hold instantly and on a launch with no network.
app.saved.entries.v1: An echo of the saves and visited tables, and the one that carries offline access, which is a paid feature. The account is the truth: CloudSync pulls at launch and pushes every change.
app.saved.saves_are_hearts_v1: A one-off migration flag: whether this phone has already cleared the saves rows the old push rule left behind. Per device by definition.

_files._why: This check reads KEYS. Two things the app keeps are files, named here so the audit is complete rather than only convenient.
_files.Application Support/catalogue: The downloaded trees, walks, species and browse feeds. Our own public data, not anything a person made, and it is what offline access is.
_files.sightings/: The photographs somebody took, which SightingSync uploads to the account's private bucket. The account is the truth: Sightings.forgetLocally() takes them off a signed-out phone and the next sign-in brings back the ones the account holds.
